title: The wary crow’s long life
literal_meaning: The wary crow lives a hundred years.
meaning_odia: ତରକିଲା କୁଆ ଶହେ ବରଷ ବଞ୍ଚେ ବୋଲି ଢଗଟି କହୁଛି। ଏଠାରେ ତରକିଲାକୁ ଚମକି ଉଠୁଥିବା ବା ସତର୍କ ରହୁଥିବା ଅର୍ଥରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ, ବିପଦ ପ୍ରତି ସଜାଗ ରହିବା ନିଜକୁ ରକ୍ଷା କରିବାରେ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରେ। ଶହେ ବରଷ କହିବାଟି ଏହି ଭାବର ଜୋର, କୁଆର ଆୟୁଷର ବୈଜ୍ଞାନିକ ହିସାବ ନୁହେଁ।
explanation: Wariness and a remarkably long life are placed together. Our editorial reading values noticing danger and responding to it, rather than dismissing every sign of caution as weakness. The hundred years is the saying’s emphatic promise, not a biological claim about crows.
usage_example: Original imagined example: A colleague pauses to check an unexpected request before acting on it and discovers a mistake. A friend recalls the wary crow to appreciate that caution.
cultural_context: The single sentence gives watchfulness a memorable reward: a whole century of life. The crow is the figure carrying that lesson; the source supplies no particular encounter or origin story.
